title: Choose the site's new visual world
question: The roll assigned the Swiss Grid Poster. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Swiss Grid Poster
options.lineage: 1950s–60s Swiss International Typographic Style concert posters
options.thesis: A decade of shipped work set as one Swiss grid poster: the facts are the composition.
options.viewport: Huge condensed 'Isaiah Mann.' on a visible grid; a full-height red field holds the dated timeline with time-proportional bars; Naru and email sit in the poster's info block.
options.risk: A grid set timidly turns into the corporate resume you ruled out; it only works at full poster scale and with the warm first-person voice.

raised.raise: Era colours travel: games, ads, enterprise and AI each own one field colour that follows them from the timeline into project tiles and project pages.
Every claim carries its proof inline: a store link, press piece, repo or dated role as a grid-aligned footnote.
Duration as data: timeline bars and project rows are sized to the real time spent.

options.label: The Discography
options.lineage: Blue Note and Factory Records catalogues
options.thesis: Every shipped project is a numbered release; Naru is the new record.
options.viewport: Black ground, the name as a label imprint, Naru as a large blue sleeve 'IM-031', older releases stacked as small colour sleeves.
options.risk: Catalogue-number portfolios are a familiar designer move, and the record metaphor can feel borrowed for an engineer.

options.label: Glazier's Wall
options.thesis: The site as one wall of glass panes: mostly clear, with one lit cobalt pane for what's happening now.
options.viewport: A black-barred grid filling the screen: the name in a big clear pane, Naru lit cobalt, each employer a pane sized by tenure.
options.case: Very clear (each pane is one destination) and nods to Seattle's glass culture; weaker on builders recognising themselves in it.
options.risk: Can read as an architecture firm's site rather than an engineer's.

options.label: Napkin Zine
options.thesis: Your career sketched like a friend explaining it on a napkin: warm, plain-spoken, and drawn.
options.viewport: A marker headline with one highlighted phrase, a doodled arrow to a hand-drawn route map of your career, and a pink 'Start with Naru' button.
options.case: Builders love engineering zines, and it matches your voice exactly; less clear as a credibility record.
options.risk: Tips into cute or gimmicky if the drawing outweighs the facts.

options.label: Teletext Service
options.thesis: The site as a teletext service: every section is a numbered page you key in.
options.viewport: Page P100: double-height name, Naru on page 200, experience rows on 300, and a red/green/yellow/blue key bar at the foot.
options.case: Speaks to your games and retro-computing roots, and the page index is very scannable; long prose reads poorly in a bitmap face.
options.risk: Reads as retro novelty if the grid isn't strict.

options.label: Endurance Livery
options.thesis: Stripes and number roundels as a portable identity across every page.
options.viewport: A powder-blue body panel with a marigold stripe running nose to tail.
options.case: Builders don't see themselves in a race garage, and the stint metaphor clouds the record.
options.kept: Era colours that travel with their work across every page.

options.label: Treasure Map
options.thesis: Navigation as inference across a weathered map.
options.viewport: A parchment coastline with coded marginalia.
options.case: Hides the facts behind puzzles: exactly the precious art piece you ruled out.
options.risk: Visitors can't find what you've built.
options.kept: Every claim carries its proof, inline.

options.label: Brine Calendar
options.thesis: Work maturing through seasons like labelled jars on a shelf.
options.case: No builder identifies with a pantry, and the jars obscure what each project is.
options.kept: Time spent is shown as data.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The clean developer portfolio, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Name and one-line pitch, two buttons, a row of project cards.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from most engineer portfolios by design.
